chapters.1: Malachi opens with God affirming his love for Israel and contrasting its future with Edom's desolation. He then rebukes the priests for offering God blemished, substandard sacrifices while reserving their best for themselves, dishonoring God's name.
chapters.2: God warns the priests that their corruption will bring curses rather than blessing, contrasting their failure with the faithfulness expected of Levi's original covenant. The chapter also condemns the people's unfaithfulness to their spouses through divorce and intermarriage with those who worship other gods.
chapters.3: God promises to send a messenger to prepare the way before him, followed by his own coming to purify and judge, especially targeting those practicing sorcery, injustice, and oppression. He also rebukes the people for withholding tithes, famously inviting them to test him by giving fully and see him pour out blessing in return.
chapters.4: The book closes with a warning of a coming "day of the Lord" that will burn up the proud and wicked like stubble, but bring healing to those who honor God's name. It ends with a promise that God will send the prophet Elijah before that great day to turn hearts toward reconciliation.
